epic.name: Hazine Experience
decisions: The controller must verify epic-hazine-preview-delivery completed and its public preview report passed before launching this epic.
Spectrum runs from the Phase 0 canonical baseline lineage in C:/Users/digit/GriotClients/Hazine.
Normalized GSAP progress is the master scroll clock and Theatre consumes that clock.
One canonical manifest owns chapter, overlay, actor-envelope, instrument, and responsive safe-zone metadata.
One selected-moment store drives story, plugin, desktop, and workbench presentations.
Claude plugin is the initial and reload-default surface.
R3F and Theatre own spatial choreography; Anime.js owns scoped DOM/SVG transformations.
Approved public/brand assets and original GLBs are immutable.

Before each story, read C:/Users/digit/.agents/skills/griot-r3f/SKILL.md and all task-relevant scene, animation, controls, loading, state, performance, and Theatre/tooling recipes; treat them as implementation requirements.
outOfScope: Production integrations, trading execution, financial advice, authentication, billing, permissions, enterprise administration, custom globe engines, and replacement brand assets
risks: Duplicated choreography tables can drift across DOM, R3F, Theatre, overlay, and navigation consumers.
Actor/UI competition can hide narrative meaning on narrow viewports.
Root-absolute URLs and route handling can fail beneath a repository subpath.
Static chapter switching can masquerade as a connected intelligence product.

stories.title: Normalize the experience clock
stories.description: As a viewer, scrolling the complete experience produces one stable progress value from 0 through 1.

steps.description: Define the normalized master progress contract in the shared store.
Drive it from the story scroll range with clamping at both bounds.
Verify monotonic 0..1 behavior at document start and end.

context.why: Every narrative system needs one authoritative clock.
risks: Competing clocks cause visual drift.
edgeCases: Zero-height or resized scroll ranges.
patterns: Use the GSAP ScrollTrigger master-clock decision from the implementation plan.

stories.title: Derive named chapter state
stories.description: As a viewer, the current named chapter is derived from one canonical ten-record experience manifest.

steps.description: Create ten stable chapter records with progress ranges.
Replace chapter-number assumptions with manifest ID lookup.
Assert IDs and ranges are unique, ordered, and complete.

context.why: Named state prevents parallel-table drift.
risks: Boundary ambiguity at adjacent ranges.
edgeCases: Exact chapter boundary progress.
patterns: Replace src/data/chapters.js parallel data with src/config/experienceManifest.js.

stories.title: Align all chapter consumers
stories.description: As a viewer, DOM copy, R3F actors, Theatre sequence, navigation, and overlays show the same current chapter and phase.

steps.description: Add overlay, actor-envelope, Theatre, and instrument references to each chapter record.
Migrate every consumer to manifest IDs.
Assert every reference resolves for all ten chapters.

context.why: The product story must read as one authored system.
risks: A stale consumer can show the wrong evidence or actor.
edgeCases: Fast scrolling across multiple chapters.
patterns: Follow src/App.jsx:16-195 and remove duplicated tables in HazineScene and LiveSystemOverlay.

stories.title: Restore deep-linked visual state
stories.description: As a visitor opening a chapter anchor directly, I arrive at that chapter's correct DOM, 3D, overlay, and instrument state.

steps.description: Resolve anchor IDs through the canonical manifest.
Set scroll and shared state after layout is ready.
Test each of the ten anchors on direct load and navigation.

context.why: Shared links must reproduce the intended story state.
risks: Anchor restoration can race scene/layout initialization.
edgeCases: Unknown anchors and reduced-motion loads.
patterns: Use stable chapter IDs, never duplicated indexes.

stories.title: Prove the Theatre integration boundary
stories.description: As a maintainer and viewer, Theatre drives at least one meaningful authored camera or scene property through a documented adapter instead of remaining a decorative clock-only dependency.

steps.description: Establish the minimal CameraDirector interface consumed by the Theatre adapter.
Create an adapter that receives normalized progress and owns Theatre sequence synchronization.
Bind at least one perceptible authored camera or scene property where Theatre adds value.
Document and test the isolated clock-only fallback so critical runtime behavior does not depend on an unused Theatre track.

context.why: The locked Theatre dependency must carry meaningful authored value or be isolated from the critical runtime.
risks: A nominal track can duplicate R3F logic or introduce two competing property owners.
edgeCases: Reduced motion, direct chapter restoration, and adapter initialization before the Theatre project is ready.
patterns: Normalized GSAP progress remains master; TheatreSequenceAdapter is the only synchronization boundary.

stories.title: Isolate story and workbench styles
stories.description: As a visitor, story, plugin, and workbench styles never change one another when routes or surfaces mount in the same application.

steps.description: Introduce explicit route/component roots and scope every story, plugin, and workbench selector beneath them.
Remove or rename colliding global selectors and generic element rules.
Load each route before and after the other and compare computed styles and screenshots for both target viewports.
Run pnpm run build after the isolation changes.

context.why: Shared global class names currently let one product surface corrupt another.
risks: Specificity increases can mask rather than remove collisions.
edgeCases: Direct workbench load, client-side route switching, and responsive media queries.
patterns: Use explicit component/route namespaces instead of ordering stylesheets for precedence.

stories.title: Guarantee manifest record parity
stories.description: As a maintainer, chapter and instrument manifests always expose the same ten resolvable records.

steps.description: Remove the legacy nine-record instrument source.
Derive chapter and instrument projections from the same ten records.
Add a build-time assertion for count and reference parity.

context.why: The current 10/9 mismatch is a structural source of drift.
risks: A derived view can silently filter a record.
edgeCases: Chapters intentionally hiding a control must still retain a manifest record.
patterns: One manifest; projections may differ, record identity may not.

stories.title: Traverse the vault door frame
stories.description: As a viewer, the camera visibly crosses the physical vault door frame while moving through the two-room model.

steps.description: Author and sample the vault spline.
Tune start, midpoint, and end camera transforms through the doorway.
Capture the three proof frames at both target viewports.

context.why: The threshold-to-treasury passage carries the narrative premise.
risks: A shortcut spline reads as a model flyover.
edgeCases: Narrow viewport clipping.
patterns: R3F/Theatre own camera choreography; CameraDirector owns the passage.

stories.title: Establish four vault compositions
stories.description: As a viewer, threshold, room one, doorway transition, and room two read as four distinct compositions.

steps.description: Assign composition beats and safe zones to manifest ranges.
Tune camera look-at and copy placement per beat.
Verify adjacent beats remain visually distinct.

context.why: Distinct rooms make spatial movement meaningful rather than decorative.
risks: Overlapping ranges collapse two rooms into one.
edgeCases: Fast scroll and mobile crop.
patterns: Use manifest safe-zone metadata and authored keyframes.

stories.title: Frame Ezgi away from camera
stories.description: As a viewer in the live-call chapter, I see Ezgi as an away-from-camera phone silhouette without product UI obscuring her.

steps.description: Adjust caller orientation and office composition.
Reserve transcript and copy safe zones.
Verify silhouette legibility at both target viewports.

context.why: Presence in the negotiation must be felt without turning Ezgi into a presenter.
risks: UI obstruction or front-facing framing breaks the scenario.
edgeCases: Mobile overlay stacking.
patterns: Use sceneProfiles responsive actor variants.

stories.title: Exit through the office window
stories.description: As a viewer, the camera travels through the office window and rises to the building exterior before geography begins.

steps.description: Author window and exterior camera keys.
Align office/building visibility to the passage.
Verify the window crossing is spatially continuous.

context.why: The wider-world transition connects the call to geography.
risks: A cut-like jump loses spatial causality.
edgeCases: Window geometry clipping.
patterns: Use CameraDirector keyframes and explicit actor envelopes.

stories.title: Dissolve building into globe
stories.description: As a viewer, the building yields to the globe through a leader/follower dissolve without both holding competing full opacity.

steps.description: Define shortened building and delayed globe envelopes.
Implement overlap budget enforcement.
Capture the transition midpoint and assert neither actor competes at full opacity.

context.why: Geography should emerge from the office context, not collide with it.
risks: Opacity overlap reads as a rendering defect.
edgeCases: Transparent materials with non-linear perceived opacity.
patterns: Apply the leader/follower hierarchy with 20-40% overlap.

stories.title: Enforce actor envelopes and UI safe zones
stories.description: As a viewer, no narrative actor reaches unintended full opacity or covers copy, transcript, or source cards outside its authored envelope.

steps.description: Encode visibility ranges and maximum overlap per actor.
Encode composition safe zones per chapter/profile.
Assert opacity and obstruction at chapter checkpoints.

context.why: Spatial priority makes the story legible.
risks: High-blast-radius actor rules affect every scene.
edgeCases: Glass actors and crossfades at exact range boundaries.
patterns: Implement ActorDirector before per-actor polish; src/components/HazineScene.jsx:22-310 is the source.

stories.title: Adapt 3D composition by aspect ratio
stories.description: As a desktop or mobile viewer, camera composition and actor framing remain intentional for my aspect ratio.

steps.description: Define desktop and mobile camera/actor profiles.
Select profiles from viewport aspect ratio.
Verify all live-intelligence phases at 1440x900 and 390x844.

context.why: Responsive 3D requires authored framing, not CSS alone.
risks: Profile switches can jump during resize.
edgeCases: Orientation change and intermediate aspect ratios.
patterns: Keep profile data in src/scene/sceneProfiles.js.

stories.title: Align a focusable seal to 3D
stories.description: As a keyboard or pointer user, the treasury seal is a focusable DOM control that stays aligned with its responsive 3D object.

steps.description: Project the seal anchor into responsive screen coordinates.
Use a semantic focusable DOM control.
Verify alignment after resize and keyboard focus.

context.why: The invitation must remain physically grounded and accessible.
risks: DOM/3D drift causes an unusable hit target.
edgeCases: Canvas resize and offscreen projection.
patterns: Use the DOM/3D state bridge rather than mesh-only interaction.

stories.title: Activate the living seal
stories.description: As a user, hover or focus signals that the seal is available and keyboard or pointer activation opens the next narrative state.

steps.description: Add hover/focus availability feedback.
Route click and keyboard activation to the same state transition.
Verify feedback begins within 150ms.

context.why: The threshold becomes an invitation rather than passive decoration.
risks: Different pointer and keyboard paths can diverge.
edgeCases: Repeated activation and focus during transition.
patterns: Use one semantic activation handler and visible focus treatment.

stories.title: Keep the seal subordinate to copy
stories.description: As a viewer before activation, the treasury seal remains visually smaller and subordinate to the chapter copy.

steps.description: Reduce the base scale per responsive profile.
Define the activated scale separately.
Review threshold screenshots for copy competition.

context.why: The seal should invite entry without overpowering the premise.
risks: Mobile scale can dominate even when desktop is balanced.
edgeCases: Large text settings.
patterns: Use scene profile values, not ad hoc viewport branches.

stories.title: Preserve seal meaning without decorative motion
stories.description: As a reduced-motion user, the seal remains understandable and activatable without rotation, bobbing, or rapid expansion.

steps.description: Gate seal motion through the shared motion policy interface.
Provide static focus and activation feedback.
Test live preference changes while the seal is visible.

context.why: Reduced motion must retain the invitation's meaning.
risks: CSS or frame-loop motion can bypass the policy.
edgeCases: Preference changes mid-animation.
patterns: Prepare for src/hooks/useMotionPolicy.js in the hardening epic.

stories.title: Present an active call
stories.description: As Ezgi, I see an active call with current speaker, timestamp, and waveform state.

steps.description: Define transcript moments with speaker and time data.
Render active speaker, elapsed time, and waveform state.
Keep playback presentation coherent across chapter changes.

context.why: Hazine begins beside a real-time negotiation, not after it.
risks: Synthetic call state can look disconnected from transcript timing.
edgeCases: Paused playback and final moment.
patterns: Replace static CSS phase switching in LiveSystemOverlay.jsx:6-123.

stories.title: Select any transcript moment
stories.description: As Ezgi, I can select every transcript moment by pointer or keyboard.

steps.description: Store selectedMomentId centrally.
Render each moment as a semantic selectable row.
Verify focus, Enter/Space, pointer, and selected state for every row.

context.why: The walkthrough must be operable, not only narrated.
risks: Rows can become pointer-only or lose focus after rerender.
edgeCases: Selecting the already-active moment.
patterns: Use Zustand shared experience state.

stories.title: Update all connected intelligence
stories.description: As Ezgi, selecting a transcript moment updates evidence, geography, relationship, confidence, and strategy in the same interaction frame.

steps.description: Attach all connected records to each moment ID.
Derive every panel from one selected moment snapshot.
Test every transcript moment for atomic visible updates.

context.why: Collect-Connect-Surface is proven only when one selection coherently changes the system.
risks: Independent subscriptions can expose mixed moment state.
edgeCases: Missing optional geography or strategy data.
patterns: Use one selected record selector; avoid chained effects.

stories.title: Persist selection across surfaces
stories.description: As Ezgi, my chosen transcript moment and connected intelligence remain selected when I switch between Claude plugin and desktop.

steps.description: Keep surface and selectedMomentId as independent store fields.
Ensure neither presentation resets selection on mount.
Toggle surfaces after every transcript selection.

context.why: One intelligence layer must survive presentation changes.
risks: Route or conditional mounting can reset local state.
edgeCases: Surface switch while playback is paused.
patterns: Shared Zustand state, never component-local selection.

stories.title: Pause autoplay on manual selection
stories.description: As Ezgi, manually selecting a transcript moment immediately pauses automatic transcript playback.

steps.description: Store playback state centrally.
Make manual selection atomically set paused state.
Verify timers cannot advance after the same interaction.

context.why: Manual inspection must not be stolen by autoplay.
risks: A pending timer can advance after pause.
edgeCases: Selection at an autoplay tick boundary.
patterns: Cancel scheduled playback before changing selectedMomentId.

stories.title: Expose required provenance fields
stories.description: As Ezgi, every consequential intelligence item exposes source or speaker, timestamp or retrieval time, lineage, taxonomy class, and confidence when applicable.

steps.description: Define the required provenance shape for consequential objects.
Populate all demo records and render inspectable receipts.
Assert 100% provenance completeness.

context.why: Provenance must precede persuasion.
risks: Optional fields can silently disappear on some record types.
edgeCases: Confidence not applicable to direct facts.
patterns: Follow PRD taxonomy FACT/SIGNAL/INTERPRETATION/HYPOTHESIS/STRATEGY.

stories.title: Trace strategy to supporting records
stories.description: As Ezgi, each surfaced strategy links back to the fact, signal, and hypothesis records supporting it.

steps.description: Store strategy support IDs.
Render lineage links and support-record inspection.
Reject dangling or wrong-taxonomy links in validation.

context.why: A strategic window is trustworthy only when its reasoning is inspectable.
risks: Broken references turn provenance into decoration.
edgeCases: A strategy supported by multiple records of one class.
patterns: Use stable record IDs and source-receipt views.

stories.title: Inspect relationship evidence
stories.description: As Ezgi, each relationship pattern exposes the prior calls or completed trades from which it was derived.

steps.description: Attach sourced interaction IDs to relationship patterns.
Expose prior-call and completed-trade receipts.
Verify every pattern has at least one inspectable source.

context.why: Persona memory must remain sourced rather than becoming an invented profile.
risks: Aggregated labels can conceal weak evidence.
edgeCases: Single-observation patterns.
patterns: Separate observed history from interpretation in the data model.

stories.title: Keep inference distinct from fact
stories.description: As Ezgi, no interpretation, hypothesis, or strategy is ever labeled or styled as a fact.

steps.description: Constrain records to the immutable five-class taxonomy.
Render explicit class labels consistently.
Add a data/UI assertion that non-facts cannot receive FACT treatment.

context.why: The system must never disguise interpretation as truth.
risks: Color-only encoding can blur class boundaries.
edgeCases: Records reclassified during knowledge transformation.
patterns: Use immutable taxonomy constants shared by data and UI.

stories.title: Default to Claude plugin
stories.description: As a first-time or reloading visitor, the product presentation opens in Claude plugin mode.

steps.description: Set plugin as the store's initial surface.
Avoid persisting desktop as a reload override.
Test fresh load and reload after desktop use.

context.why: Plugin first is a locked product decision.
risks: Persisted UI state can violate the default.
edgeCases: Reload during a selected moment.
patterns: Selection may persist during live switching; surface resets on reload.

stories.title: Present focused plugin context
stories.description: As Ezgi in plugin mode, I see an embedded companion focused on the live decision context.

steps.description: Define plugin-specific information hierarchy.
Render only focused context and necessary controls.
Verify it reads as embedded rather than a shrunken desktop.

context.why: The plugin supports the conversation without replacing it.
risks: Feature parity can produce a cramped dashboard.
edgeCases: Long provenance labels in the narrow frame.
patterns: Differentiate information architecture, not only rail visibility.

stories.title: Present the expanded desktop treasury
stories.description: As Ezgi in desktop mode, I see the full navigation rail and a larger working surface.

steps.description: Define desktop-specific information hierarchy.
Expose full rail and expanded panels.
Verify selected data matches plugin mode exactly.

context.why: Desktop expands the same intelligence into a larger treasury.
risks: A separate presentation can drift into separate data.
edgeCases: Switching at mobile widths.
patterns: Both surfaces consume the same selected record.

stories.title: Share one intelligence model
stories.description: As Ezgi, plugin, desktop, story overlay, and workbench present the same data and selection state.

steps.description: Remove duplicate route-specific meeting data.
Expose route-safe shared selectors.
Compare record IDs and selection across every presentation.

context.why: One intelligence layer across surfaces is a core thesis.
risks: Route-specific stores can diverge on refresh.
edgeCases: Workbench direct load without story initialization.
patterns: Reuse src/data/liveMeeting.js and a route-safe shared store slice.

stories.title: Select raw knowledge fragments
stories.description: As Ezgi, I can select raw meeting, market, research, and relationship fragments.

steps.description: Define selectable fragments across all four source kinds.
Add semantic pointer/keyboard selection.
Verify selection feedback for every fragment.

context.why: Users must manipulate the raw material of the treasury.
risks: Source-kind styling can imply taxonomy class.
edgeCases: Multiple fragments from the same source.
patterns: Use liveMeeting stable IDs and KnowledgeTransform.jsx:18-52.

stories.title: Assemble connected intelligence visibly
stories.description: As Ezgi, selecting fragments visibly assembles a source receipt, relationship memory, classification, and strategy.

steps.description: Map selected fragments to each assembled output.
Render the four-stage result with lineage retained.
Verify assembly for each source-kind selection.

context.why: The Collect-Connect-Surface transformation must be directly legible.
risks: Animation can obscure which source produced which result.
edgeCases: A fragment without relationship history.
patterns: Keep provenance visible throughout transformation.

stories.title: Animate scoped knowledge transformations
stories.description: As Ezgi, DOM and connected-line motion shows how selected information changes form without leaking animation state to other components.

steps.description: Scope Anime.js targets to each component root.
Implement replay and cancellation on selection changes.
Route timing and reduced motion through shared policy inputs.

context.why: Motion explains transformation rather than decorating it.
risks: Global selectors can animate the wrong surface.
edgeCases: Rapid repeated selection and unmount during animation.
patterns: Anime.js owns DOM/SVG; use root scoping, cancellation, and replay semantics.

stories.title: Inspect every taxonomy layer
stories.description: As Ezgi, I can directly inspect FACT, SIGNAL, INTERPRETATION, HYPOTHESIS, and STRATEGY layers without losing lineage.

steps.description: Expose one inspectable control for each immutable class.
Show source and parent lineage in every class view.
Verify all five classes and transitions.

context.why: Explicit taxonomy protects epistemic integrity.
risks: Collapsed layers can conceal inference.
edgeCases: A class with no selected-moment record.
patterns: Keep class labels textual, not color-only.

stories.title: Apply the Hazine workbench system
stories.description: As a /workbench user, I see the approved light ivory center workspace, dark rails, typography, and restrained Hazine accents.

steps.description: Rebuild the workbench layout with dark rails and ivory center.
Apply approved typography and semantic gold/green accents.
Capture desktop and mobile workbench proofs.

context.why: Workbench must be a deeper Hazine surface, not a separate prototype.
risks: Global selectors can contaminate the story.
edgeCases: Transparent content over dark/luminous scene regions.
patterns: Scope workbench selectors; follow src/workbench/workbench.css:1-160.

stories.title: Drive every workbench panel from selection
stories.description: As a workbench user, transcript selection drives Live Intelligence, Evidence, Relationship, confidence, geography, and strategy panels rather than only a headline.

steps.description: Bind every panel to the shared selected record.
Remove static panel placeholders.
Validate all panel states for every transcript moment.

context.why: The workbench is the strongest operational proof of connected intelligence.
risks: One stale panel breaks the single-state model.
edgeCases: Direct workbench load before playback begins.
patterns: Reuse the selector proven in STORY-021.

stories.title: Inspect workbench receipts and lineage
stories.description: As a workbench user, evidence and relationship views change with selection and let me inspect source receipts and strategy lineage.

steps.description: Add source-receipt inspection to evidence views.
Add sourced-call/trade inspection to relationship views.
Add supporting-record inspection to strategy views.

context.why: A larger treasury surface should deepen provenance inspection.
risks: Nested inspection can obscure the live-call context.
edgeCases: Missing optional receipt metadata.
patterns: Reuse stable provenance IDs from STORY-024 through STORY-026.

stories.title: Render the desktop chapter instrument
stories.description: As a desktop viewer, I navigate with a vertical chapter instrument rail.

steps.description: Render chapter controls from the manifest.
Connect each control to stable chapter navigation.
Verify current and focus states at desktop size.

context.why: The rail makes the long-form experience operable.
risks: Rail indexes can drift from chapter IDs.
edgeCases: Keyboard navigation during smooth scrolling.
patterns: Refactor InstrumentRail.jsx:4-43 to consume the manifest.

stories.title: Render the mobile bottom island
stories.description: As a mobile viewer, I navigate with a horizontal bottom island that respects the device safe area.

steps.description: Switch the instrument to horizontal mobile presentation.
Apply safe-area inset spacing.
Verify reachability, focus, and no content obstruction at 390x844.

context.why: Mobile choreography needs a purpose-built control surface.
risks: The island can cover transcript actions.
edgeCases: Devices with zero or large safe-area insets.
patterns: Use CSS env(safe-area-inset-bottom).

stories.title: Synchronize chapter instrument feedback
stories.description: As a viewer, current chapter, normalized progress, and a short system observation update together.

steps.description: Add concise observation copy to manifest records.
Select chapter, progress, and observation from one state snapshot.
Verify synchronized updates during fast scroll and anchor jumps.

context.why: The instrument should report one coherent system state.
risks: Independent animations can make labels lag progress.
edgeCases: Exact chapter transitions.
patterns: Derive all three values from the canonical manifest and master clock.

stories.title: Resolve all ten chapter states
stories.description: As a reviewer, each of the ten chapters resolves to its correct DOM, 3D, overlay, Theatre, and instrument state.

steps.description: Enumerate the ten stable chapter IDs and expected consumer state for each.
Exercise scroll and direct-anchor entry for every chapter.
Correct any consumer mismatch and rerun the full ten-chapter matrix.

context.why: The full experience is only coherent when every consumer agrees in every chapter.
risks: Testing only sequential scroll can miss direct-entry initialization defects.
edgeCases: Exact boundaries, fast multi-chapter scroll, direct anchor, and reduced-motion state.
patterns: Validate projections from the canonical manifest; never patch a consumer-specific table.
